subject: Term adjustment & throughput uplift for EdgeCommerce Hosted API
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@edgecommerce.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity and term question

Hi Sofia —

Hope you’re well. We’re launching a personalization push in Q3 and we’re seeing a sustained uptick in model usage during early tests. Current hosted plan (750M tokens/mo) is not going to be sufficient — we need guidance on a path to ~1.8B tokens/mo with predictable latency and soft-burst capacity for campaigns.

Specific asks:
- Can you outline available month-to-month vs committed-month pricing for that scale?
- What happens to per-second rate limits and burst windows if we move up a commit tier?
- Are there any short-term term changes (mid-contract) we should expect to renegotiate?

I attached a quick spreadsheet with projected usage (EdgeCommerce_commit_request.xlsx). Also looping in Raj (ops) for traffic numbers. We’re hoping to have a decision and signed amendment by end of May if possible.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Product
EdgeCommerce
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity and term question

Tara — thanks for the note and the file. Quick read-through: your projected monthly token profile (peaks in campaign windows) maps well to a staged commit increase. Before we draft an amendment I need a small traffic snapshot (peak RPS, median sequence length, percent of traffic in 10-min bursts) — Raj, if you can drop that below that helps accelerate ops sizing.

High-level proposal to start:
- Move from 750M -> 2B monthly committed tokens (12-month term) with a 3-month ramp (750M -> 1.5B -> 2B).
- Premier hosted tier (adds 2x burst window for 10mins and a higher soft-rate band). This changes your per-route rate limits from 20 RPS -> 50 RPS for API keys in the renewed route group.
- Pricing: incremental commit tier priced at $0.60 per 1K tokens for the delta after existing commit (we’ll put exact numbers into an amendment).
- Soft-throttle behavior: requests that exceed real-time rate bands are queued up to the burst window; sustained overages billed as overage at a reduced uplift.

Next steps I propose:
1) Raj provides the small traffic snapshot and the spreadsheet of expected monthly profiles (by day)
2) Karthik will propose the ops config and any recommended caching/batching knobs
3) We’ll produce a short amendment (proposed-amendment_v2.pdf) with term, pricing, and a staged ramp schedule for signature.

I’ve attached a template amendment and put a slot on my calendar for Tuesday 10am PT if you’d like to review the numbers live.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@edgecommerce.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@edgecommerce.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity and term question

Thanks Sofia. Quick snapshot below (pasted from our observability):
- Current committed: 750M tokens/mo (production).
- Recent 7-day median RPS: 12 RPS. Peak 10-min window: 68 RPS.
- Median sequence length: ~120 tokens. Peak campaigns move average to ~380 tokens (longer prompts + history).
- Error profile: we saw ~0.8% 429 rate during the two peaks last week (campaign sends).

Attached small CSV with per-hour rollup (EdgeCommerce_usage_snapshot.csv).

We’re comfortable with a staged ramp. Our procurement window needs a signed amendment + PO to start the ramp formally. If you can lay out a pro-rated billing plan for the ramp, that’ll help procurement sign off.

— Raj
Engineering Ops, EdgeCommerce
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@edgecommerce.com>, Tara Singh <tara@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity and term question

Raj / Tara — thanks for the numbers, that peak morphology explains the 429s. Operational notes and a recommended configuration: 

- Suggested commitment: reserve 2.0B tokens/mo with a 3-month ramp (as Sofia suggested). Rationale: it gives headroom for campaign peaks while keeping per-token economics favorable.
- Rate limits and burst: move to Premier route group limits (50 RPS per route key) + a 10-minute burst multiplier of 2.0x. During bursts we use priority queueing for in-flight requests and elastic token-bucket smoothing to avoid sudden 429 storms.
- Latency SLA: we can commit to p95 < 220ms for generation calls under committed throughput; sustained overages fall into the soft-overage SLA.
- Cost mechanics: pro-rated billing on ramp months. Example (simple): May (remaining days) prorated at 40% of new tier, June at 70% while ramping to full 100% in July. Early termination clause: 90-day notice with early-exit credit equal to unused committed tokens * 50% refund credit to be applied to final invoice.
- Ops handoffs: enable prefix caching on stable prompts and enable a 30s KV cache for session tokens — can lower token usage by ~6–12% on our tests.

I attached the draft amendment with the pricing table and ramp schedule (proposed-amendment_v2.pdf).

If this looks OK we can mark it as redline-ready and Sofia can send to procurement. I can join a PO/contract call if procurement needs technical confirmation.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Billing: pro-rated ramp billing; final numbers in proposed-amendment_v2.pdf.
